## Correction after reporter follow-up — ENOSPC deprioritized

The reporter says the affected Mac had adequate free space. Treat ENOSPC as **unsupported for this occurrence**, not as the leading explanation.

There is also an important pipeline correction. On the exact baseline (`v0.12.10`, Electron `33.4.11`), this error occurs in the in-process native Squirrel updater **before ShipIt installation**:

1. Squirrel downloads the ZIP from electron-updater's loopback proxy.
2. It writes the ZIP atomically and runs `ditto -xk`.
3. Electron's Squirrel patch validates the extracted app with `kSecCSCheckNestedCode | kSecCSStrictValidate | kSecCSCheckAllArchitectures`.
4. Only after validation passes does it write the ShipIt request and launch ShipIt.

Therefore `ShipIt_stderr.log` is not expected to contain this failure. The `.ShipIt/update.*` path is merely Squirrel's staging location.

The generic root-app message also does **not** prove the root executable itself was unsigned. Strict nested validation can return `errSecCSUnsigned` for a nested code object while Squirrel's outer message names the root `.app`. AO currently surfaces only `Error.message`, losing the underlying Security.framework error that can identify the failing subcomponent.

### What remains established

- Both exact published ZIPs match their GitHub digests and feed hashes.
- Both survive `ditto -x -k`, strict/deep codesign validation, Gatekeeper, and stapler verification.
- The release signing runner was macOS 26.6.2, so this is not merely a modern-macOS validation rule missed by an old CI host.
- The public release did not exist until after signing and verification, ruling out an unsigned draft asset being cached from the public feed.

### Current leading hypotheses

1. **v0.12.10 re-staging/cache race.** This baseline predates [PR #4849](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4849), which documents that each 15-minute Nightly check re-copied the cached ZIP and handed Squirrel another install request (526 requests observed for 10 installs). A manual check could also arrive while native staging/verification is still settling.
2. **A user-local extraction or endpoint-security modification** caused one nested executable/framework in the staged tree to differ from the hash-verified ZIP.
3. **A stale staged build** was validated instead of the Nightly displayed as the home channel. v0.12.10 did not persist staged provenance and could not cancel a build already handed to Squirrel; #4849 fixed those gaps.

These are hypotheses, not yet a claimed root cause. Architecture mismatch is low probability because both architectures are signed with the same requirement, and the feed selects architecture explicitly.

Ran with **adequate free disk throughout (>9 GB)**, in a fully isolated environment (separate `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `AO_DATA_DIR`, `AO_RUN_FILE`, Electron `userData`, updater cache and ShipIt cache, launched via `env -i`). Production AO data, the installed app and the real updater cache were never touched.

**Headline: low disk space is ruled out as the mechanism — provably, not just unconfirmed.** Correcting my earlier framing in this thread.

### 1. Published artifact re-verified independently

Fresh download of `Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.12.11-nightly.202609052046.zip`:

- size `176688854` — matches `nightly-mac.yml` exactly
- SHA-512 `RQ/iTIQvANcRTh2fVcrreeDJbtH0frfxXSj29V7apvaIu3DKu17lb6JApL8hNBYqIsNnetoZbGMEB354ojNBqA==` — matches the feed exactly
- `ditto -x -k` → rc 0; `codesign --verify --deep --strict` → rc 0
- **passes `codesign -R` against the running app's designated requirement** (the requirement ShipIt actually validates against), `stapler validate` OK, `spctl` accepted as *Notarized Developer ID*

No packaging or signing change is warranted.

### 2. The error detail is diagnostic, and the two reports are different failures

`SQRLCodeSignature.m` supplies the `Code signature at URL %@ did not pass validation` prefix; everything after the colon is the Security-framework result. Mutating the verified bundle one way at a time:

| Mutation of staged bundle | codesign result |
|---|---|
| none (control) | **passes** |
| all xattrs stripped | **passes** |
| `_CodeSignature/` removed | `invalid resource directory` |
| main executable truncated 50% | `invalid or unsupported format for signature` |
| main executable truncated 99% | `main executable failed strict validation` |
| **main executable zero-length** | **`code object is not signed at all`** |
| **main executable deleted** | **`code object is not signed at all`** |
| `Contents/MacOS/` removed | `code object is not signed at all` |
| whole `Contents/` emptied | `bundle format unrecognized` |

So this report means precisely: **the staged bundle kept its structure but `Contents/MacOS/agent-orchestrator` is missing or zero-length.**

That is *not* the same failure as the original v0.10.0 report in the issue body (`code failed to satisfy specified code requirement(s)` = a seal/requirement failure). The AppleDouble/symlink seal theory does not explain this one.

### 3. Why truncation — and therefore ENOSPC — cannot produce it

Entry order in the published ZIP (7,152 files):

| Entry | Position |
|---|---|
| `Contents/_CodeSignature/CodeResources` | **#5** |
| `Contents/MacOS/agent-orchestrator` | **#7** |
| `Contents/Info.plist` | **#7,151 (last)** |

The main executable comes out essentially first and `Info.plist` last, so any short read loses `Info.plist` and *keeps* the executable — the exact opposite of what was observed. Confirmed empirically: `ditto -x -k` on a 116 MB prefix of the 176 MB ZIP yielded a full 69,632-byte `MacOS/agent-orchestrator` and no `Info.plist`, and codesign reported `bundle format unrecognized, invalid, or unsuitable`.

Independently: `ditto` exits non-zero on a short ZIP (`Couldn't read pkzip signature`) and Squirrel captures that as `SQRLZipArchiverExitCodeErrorKey`, so a truncated download surfaces as a **ZIP error, never a signature error**.

**Therefore the extraction completed (ditto exited 0, `Info.plist` present) and the main executable was removed or zeroed afterwards** — post-extraction mutation of `~/Library/Caches/dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop.ShipIt/update.XXXX/`.

A free-space preflight would not have prevented this instance.

### 4. Other prioritized hypotheses

- **Architecture / feed selection — sound.** `MacUpdater.filterFilesForArch` selects on the `arm64` filename substring; the feed lists both slices with correct sizes/hashes; an arm64 host picks arm64 (logged in my isolated run). Rosetta hosts deliberately take arm64 too.
- **Designated requirement drift — none.** Running app's DR is the standard Developer ID form (`X9LNSP8MC2`); the fresh nightly validates against it.
- **Quarantine / translocation — not implicated.** Installed app has no `com.apple.quarantine` and is not translocated; ShipIt clears quarantine itself (`clearQuarantineForDirectory:`); stripping every xattr still verifies clean.
- **Cached/staged artifact identity — the real exposure.** `DownloadedUpdateHelper.validateDownloadedPath` reuses the cached ZIP on **existence alone** within a running process (its own comment: *"check here only existence, not checksum"*), and `updateDownloaded` serves it to Squirrel with `Content-Length` taken from the **feed** (`zipFileInfo.info.size`), never from the file on disk. Nothing re-hashes between "verified download" and "handed to Squirrel", so a mutated staged copy is replayed forever.

### 5. Not reproduced, and one thing worth its own issue

The hop **succeeds** on a healthy machine — 5/5 successful ShipIt installs here over 5 days, including this exact hop. The mutation is environmental (a concurrent staging cleanup, or an external agent touching `~/Library/Caches`, both fit the signature).

Separately reproduced and worth tracking on its own: **142 ShipIt relaunches in ~5 minutes**, each failing `Could not read update request` / `ShipItState.plist … no such file`, and **each relaunch truncates `ShipIt_stderr.log`**. That is why reports in this family only ever carry the *last* error and never the first one's cause — the diagnostic destroys itself, which is exactly why #3034 and #4175 were so hard to pin down. Combined with the note at `auto-updater.ts:1240` that a cache hit "hands Squirrel a fresh install request", concurrent installers sharing one staging directory is a plausible in-house trigger for the post-extraction removal — flagged, not claimed, since I have not reproduced it.

### 6. Fix

PR #4981 implements item 4 of the triage list above (discard the failed update's staging/cache material before a full re-download) plus the missing regression coverage:

- On an install rejection, disarm the staged build and drop electron-updater's cached pending download, so the next check is a real download-and-verify instead of a replay of the same bytes. Cause-agnostic, which matters given the trigger is environmental.
- Restore the `AO_E2E_UPDATE_SENTINEL` listener that #3294 added and an unrelated reformat in #3012 (`9caafbee8`, 2026-07-31) deleted. Because `assertSentinelCapable` only inspects a *built* `app.asar` and fails by *refusing to run*, the macOS update-hop job has been silently unrunnable against **any** baseline for five weeks. A unit test now pins the coupling.

Deliberately **not** included: a free-space preflight (ruled out above), the direct-download remediation UI (#3528), and adding baselines to the hop matrix (#3288 — note v0.10.0 can never satisfy `assertSentinelCapable`, so it needs a different staging signal first).

### Evidence still worth collecting from the affected Mac

Since ENOSPC is out, the useful evidence changes. Before clearing the cache:

```bash
ls -la ~/Library/Caches/dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop.ShipIt/update.*/Agent*.app/Contents/MacOS/
system_profiler SPInstallHistoryDataType | grep -iE "protect|crowdstrike|sentinel|sophos|jamf"
log show --last 2h --predicate 'subsystem == "com.apple.xprotect"' 2>/dev/null | tail -50
```

The first line is the decisive one: a zero-length or absent `agent-orchestrator` in the staging dir confirms this analysis directly.

## Correction + follow-up: nested code objects, the #4849 lineage, and a feature-pin display bug

Testing the hypotheses raised rather than assuming them. One of them **corrects my previous comment**, and together they produce a complete causal chain.

### 1. Correction: my previous narrowing was wrong

I claimed the error means the *root* executable is missing or zero-length. That is too narrow — the `kSecCSCheckNestedCode` point is right. Retested:

| Mutation of the verified bundle | codesign result |
|---|---|
| nested **helper app** executable removed | **`code object is not signed at all`** — reported *against the root*, `In subcomponent: …/Agent Orchestrator Helper.app` |
| `Squirrel.framework` binary removed | **`code object is not signed at all`** — `In subcomponent: …/Squirrel.framework` |
| `Electron Framework` binary removed | **`code object is not signed at all`** — `In subcomponent: …/Electron Framework.framework` |
| root main executable removed / zero-length | `code object is not signed at all` |
| `Resources/daemon/ao` zeroed | `a sealed resource is missing or invalid` |
| `Resources/tmux/bin/tmux` zeroed | `a sealed resource is missing or invalid` |
| `Resources/agent-browser/agent-browser` zeroed | `a sealed resource is missing or invalid` |

Since `SQRLCodeSignature` formats its message with the URL it was handed, the root URL in the report says nothing about *which* object failed. So the correct reading is:

> **Any code object in the staged bundle — root executable, a helper `.app`, or a framework — is missing or unsigned.**

Note the sharp split: **nested code objects** give this error; **sealed resources** (the bundled daemon, tmux, agent-browser binaries) give a different one. That still excludes a large class of partial-extraction shapes, and my ZIP-entry-order evidence ruling out truncation/ENOSPC stands unchanged.

### 2. The trigger: v0.12.10 predates #4849

This is the piece that ties it together. Verified by lineage, not assumption:

```
v0.12.10                published 2026-08-31T05:19:26Z
190df05fc (#4849)       merged    2026-09-05 02:16
git merge-base --is-ancestor 190df05fc v0.12.10  -> NO   (v0.12.10 lacks the fix)
git merge-base --is-ancestor 190df05fc 7e8a66229 -> YES  (the offered nightly has it)
```

#4849's own live measurements on a pre-fix install: a Squirrel install request **every 15 minutes** — 41 on Sep 1, 36 on Sep 2, **526 total against 10 actual installs since Jul 4** — with `update.zip` rewritten in full (174,750,820 bytes) and ShipIt logging the next install request 3 seconds later.

So the affected v0.12.10 machine was re-extracting ~175 MB into a fresh `update.XXXX/` under one shared `~/Library/Caches/dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop.ShipIt/`, then verifying it, **every 15 minutes, indefinitely, while the user sat on a staged build**. Overlapping extract → verify → cleanup cycles sharing one staging root is a mechanism that can leave a tree whose nested code objects are gone while its structure survives — which is exactly the signature in §1. It also explains the intermittency and the self-healing in #4175.

Consistent with my own isolated repro of **142 ShipIt relaunches in ~5 minutes**, and with this machine's 5/5 successful installs on a build that *has* #4849.

**The chicken-and-egg worth calling out:** #4849 fixes the trigger, but it is undeliverable to precisely the population that needs it, because receiving it requires the update that is failing. A stranded v0.12.10 user cannot reach the fix by updating. That makes a recovery path (discard the staged copy and re-download, plus a manual-install route) necessary rather than merely defensive.

### 3. Ruled out: unsigned feature build behind a "Nightly" dropdown

Checked directly. Pulled the first 8 MB of `Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.12.0-pr4562.202608280157.zip` and inspected the main executable:

```
Identifier=dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop
Authority=Developer ID Application: Prateek Karnal (X9LNSP8MC2)
TeamIdentifier=X9LNSP8MC2
flags=0x10000(runtime)
```

Feature builds are properly Developer ID signed with the same identity, and carry `_CodeSignature/CodeResources`. An effective feature pin therefore does **not** explain an unsigned staged object. Hypothesis closed.

### 4. But a real bug fell out of checking it

`UpdatesSection.tsx:159`:

```ts
const primaryValue: PrimaryValue =
  developerMode && (form.feature !== null || showFeature) ? "feature" : form.channel;
```

and `auto-updater.ts` `configureFeed` gives the pin absolute priority:

```ts

```

With `developerMode` off, a non-null `feature` pin is ignored **for display** and the dropdown renders `form.channel` — so Settings can read **"Nightly (pre-release)"** while the updater is actually pinned to a `pr<N>` feed. There is a `PR #<n>` badge elsewhere on the page, so it is not fully hidden, but the channel control itself is misleading. Not this bug's cause; worth its own issue.

Practical consequence for triage here: **the "Candidate release: v0.12.11-nightly.202609052046" in the report above was inferred from the channel, not observed** — the evidence-needed list in that same comment asks for the target version precisely because it was not supplied. ### 5. Where this leaves the fix

PR #4981 is unchanged in substance and is the right layer: on an install rejection it disarms the staged build and drops electron-updater's cached pending download, so the next check is a real download-and-verify rather than a replay of the same bytes. That is cause-agnostic, which matters because the trigger is a race rather than a deterministic input — and it is the only thing that helps a v0.12.10 user who cannot receive #4849.

Its regression-coverage half also restores the `AO_E2E_UPDATE_SENTINEL` listener deleted by #3012, which had left the macOS update-hop job unrunnable against any baseline since 2026-07-31.

Still **not** included, deliberately: a free-space preflight (ruled out), direct-download remediation UI (#3528), and hop-matrix baselines (#3288).

## Squirrel flag set verified at source — and it does **not** discriminate. Plus a correction to my own coverage claim.

### 1. The flag pin is correct — confirmed at source

Fetched the pinned commit directly:

```
Squirrel.Mac @0e5d146ba13101a1302d59ea6e6e0b3cace4ae38 — SQRLCodeSignature.m:127
result = SecStaticCodeCheckValidityWithErrors(staticCode,
             kSecCSCheckAllArchitectures,
             (__bridge SecRequirementRef)self.requirement, &validityError);
```

`kSecCSCheckAllArchitectures` only — no `kSecCSCheckNestedCode`, no `kSecCSStrictValidate`. Confirmed. (Line 50/80 also confirm the requirement is `SecCodeCopyDesignatedRequirement` of the **running** app, via `SecCodeCopySelf`.)

### 2. But the inference from it does not hold — tested against the real API

`codesign(1)` applies its own defaults and cannot answer this, so I built a small harness that calls `SecStaticCodeCheckValidityWithErrors` with exactly the flags above and the running app's designated requirement, then mutated the verified bundle one way at a time:

| Mutation | `0x1` allArch only (Squirrel @0e5d146) | `0x9` +nested (current main) |
|---|---|---|
| control | PASS | PASS |
| root executable removed | **-67062** | -67062 |
| root executable zero-length | **-67062** | -67062 |
| **helper `.app` executable removed** | **-67062** | -67062 |
| **`Electron Framework` binary removed** | **-67062** | -67062 |
| `_CodeSignature/` removed | -67023 | -67023 |
| `Resources/daemon/ao` zeroed | -67054 | -67054 |

`-67062` = `errSecCSUnsigned` = *"code object is not signed at all"*; `-67054` = `errSecCSBadResource`; `-67023` = invalid resource directory.

**The two flag sets give identical results.** Dropping `kSecCSCheckNestedCode` does not stop a missing helper-app or framework binary from surfacing as `errSecCSUnsigned` at the root URL — nested *code objects* are reached through resource-seal validation regardless, which is why they differ from plain sealed resources like the bundled `daemon/ao` and `tmux`.

So the correct scope is unchanged from my last comment, and it is now established by the actual API under the actual flags rather than by the CLI:

> **The staged bundle's root code object, or a nested helper `.app`/framework binary, is missing or unsigned.** Sealed resources and seal damage are excluded — they produce different OSStatus values.

I'm not claiming which of those it was; I'm saying the error cannot distinguish them, so evidence from the affected machine is still required.

### 3. Correction to my own claim about e2e coverage

I said the update-hop job had been "unrunnable against **any** baseline". That was too strong. The capability check inspects the **baseline** bundle, so baselines published *before* #3012 still carry the listener and still work.

The two runs that have ever existed — both 2026-08-02, four minutes apart — show this precisely:

| Run | Baseline | Published | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `30758412650` | `v0.11.2-nightly.202608011442` | Aug 1 (**after** #3012) | **failed** — `baseline … has no AO_E2E_UPDATE_SENTINEL listener` |
| `30758538690` | `v0.11.2-nightly.202607301613` | Jul 30 (**before** #3012) | success |

Accurate statement: **the job works only with baselines published before 2026-07-31, and fails against every baseline since — including v0.12.10, the one this issue is about.** Confirmed: no run covers v0.12.10 → current nightly; those two are the only runs in the workflow's history.

### 4. That failure also misdirected the operator, now fixed

The check's message said *"pick a baseline released **after** it"*. When the listener has been deleted from the app, that is exactly backwards — every newer baseline fails, and moving newer makes it worse. Run `30758412650` is that mistake happening for real; the operator recovered by going *older*, against the advice.

Pushed to PR #4981: the message now names both causes and which direction each implies, and cites those two runs so the next person doesn't repeat it.

### 5. Still open, per your steer

- **Repeated-request path** — strongest remaining lead. v0.12.10 lacks #4849 (verified: `merge-base --is-ancestor 190df05fc v0.12.10` → NO), so it re-stages and issues a Squirrel install request every 15 minutes indefinitely. Not yet reproduced as a race; this machine has the fix, so it cannot exhibit it.
- **Stale staging** — §6 of #4849 notes staged provenance did not survive a restart before that PR, so a v0.12.10 install could come back armed with a build it no longer tracks. Worth testing against a v0.12.10 baseline specifically.
- **Feature pin** — ruled out as a signing cause (feature builds are Developer ID signed), but the display divergence at `UpdatesSection.tsx:159` stands and still means the staged build on that machine is unconfirmed.

## Interim evidence report — v0.12.10 → nightly, run in isolation. Plus a correction to my Squirrel flags claim.

### 0. Correction first: my flag-set claim was wrong

I quoted upstream Squirrel.Mac `@0e5d146` (`kSecCSCheckAllArchitectures` only). **Electron v33.4.11 patches that.** `patches/squirrel.mac/.patches` lists `fix_use_kseccschecknestedcode_kseccsstrictvalidate_in_the_sec.patch`, which rewrites the call to:

```objc
SecStaticCodeCheckValidityWithErrors(staticCode,
    kSecCSCheckNestedCode | kSecCSStrictValidate | kSecCSCheckAllArchitectures,
    (__bridge SecRequirementRef)self.requirement, &validityError);   // = 0x19
```

The patch's stated purpose is exactly "to ensure Squirrel.Mac validates the nested bundles (nested Frameworks) including the incoming Squirrel.Mac framework." I read the wrong copy; that's on me. PR body, issue narrative and the test rationale in code are all corrected.

**The mutation results are unaffected** — re-ran the whole matrix under `0x1`, `0x9` and the effective `0x19`; all three are identical (table in the PR). Root executable *or* nested helper/framework binary missing → `-67062 errSecCSUnsigned`; seal damage → `-67023`; sealed resources → `-67054`.

---

### 1. Exact target resolved by v0.12.10

Real v0.12.10 baseline, Nightly channel, live feed, fully isolated:

```
Found version 0.12.11-nightly.202609052046
  (url: Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.12.11-nightly.202609052046.zip,
        Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-x64-0.12.11-nightly.202609052046.zip)
Downloading update from Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.12.11-nightly.202609052046.zip
```

**arm64 slice selected correctly.** So the "Candidate release" in the original report was inferred but is **correct** — v0.12.10 on Nightly does resolve exactly that build. (Also confirmed: the `AO_E2E_UPDATE_SENTINEL` string is absent from v0.12.10's `app.asar`.)

### 2. Does the hop reproduce? **No — it succeeded.**

`Installation completed successfully` at 17:45:07; the bundle ended on `0.12.11-nightly.202609052046`. A clean v0.12.10 → nightly hop works. Whatever the affected user hit is **not** deterministic in this path.

### 3. Can repeated check/download operations replace or corrupt the staging directory? **Yes — demonstrated.**

This is the finding. Sampling `~/Library/Caches/dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop.ShipIt/` once a second:

```
17:24:54  update.okxiJh2  exe=69632   helper=ABSENT   fw=0  plist=ABSENT   <- extracting
17:24:56  update.okxiJh2  exe=69632   helper=122000   fw=2  plist=ABSENT   <- extracting
17:24:57  update.okxiJh2  exe=69632   helper=122000   fw=8  plist=ok       <- COMPLETE, valid
17:39:57  update.okxiJh2  exe=ABSENT  helper=122000   fw=8  plist=ok       <- *** EXECUTABLE GONE ***
17:39:58  update.4hDq9mS  exe=69632   helper=ABSENT   fw=0  plist=ABSENT   <- next request stages afresh
17:40:00  update.4hDq9mS  exe=69632   helper=122000   fw=8  plist=ok
```

At **17:39:57** — 15 minutes to the second after the first staging, one second before the next request created a new directory — the *completed* staging directory had its **main executable removed while `Info.plist`, the helper apps and all 8 frameworks were still present**.

That is byte-for-byte the `root executable removed` row of the mutation matrix: **precisely the state that returns `errSecCSUnsigned` = "code object is not signed at all"** under the effective `0x19` flags.

**9 install requests in ~20 minutes** on this baseline, consistent with #4849's measured 526-against-10.

So: the pre-#4849 repeated-request loop **does** transiently replace/corrupt the native updater staging directory, and the transient state it passes through is exactly the one this bug reports.

### What is still not proven

I did **not** observe a verification landing inside that window — this run installed successfully. So:

- **Reproduced:** the corrupt staging state, and the race window that creates it, on a real v0.12.10 against the live feed.
- **Not reproduced:** the collision itself (verify landing while the executable is absent). That is timing-dependent, which fits the intermittency here and the self-healing in #4175.

I'd now call the mechanism **strongly evidenced rather than confirmed**: v0.12.10 lacks #4849 (`merge-base --is-ancestor 190df05fc v0.12.10` → NO), re-stages every 15 minutes, and each cycle passes through a staging state that verifies as `errSecCSUnsigned`.

### Practical consequences

1. **#4849 fixes the trigger** by suspending auto-download for an already-staged build — but it is undeliverable to the affected population, since receiving it requires the update that is failing. A stranded v0.12.10 user cannot reach it by updating.
2. **PR #4981 is therefore the operative fix for existing installs**: on an install rejection it disarms the staged build and drops the cached download, so the next check re-downloads and re-verifies instead of replaying. Cause-agnostic, which matters for a race.
3. The single decisive artifact from the affected Mac remains a listing of `~/Library/Caches/dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop.ShipIt/update.*/Agent*.app/Contents/MacOS/` — an absent or zero-length `agent-orchestrator` under an otherwise intact bundle confirms this outright.

## Prior-art review before asking for more implementation effort — direction question for maintainers

I moved #4968 to **draft** while this is decided. I went back through the tracker and the code, and I want to surface history I had not fully engaged with when filing this, plus one defect in my own PR.

**This feature has shipped twice and been removed twice, deliberately.**

- #2836 (merged 2026-07-22) added a durable worker-idle → orchestrator outbox. Removed in full by #3257 per #3038: it re-fired for the same worker, *idle does not mean done*, and each nudge burned an orchestrator turn on state the sidebar already showed.
- #3274 (merged 2026-07-29, released in `v0.11.2`) is the closer precedent, and I did not cite it in the PR. It was already the bounded design — delay before re-engaging, exponential backoff, a hard three-attempt ceiling, deferral while an unread human notification existed, and `ao orchestrator done` for durable completion. It was reverted two days later by #3394, with the stated reason that orchestrators received the daemon-authored message "3 to 4 duplicates in a row" and that "the decision is to drop the feature entirely rather than tune it."

Read together, the objection was not delivery reliability. It was that unsolicited daemon-authored turns cost orchestrator turns and can contaminate orchestrator context. A more durable outbox does not answer that objection by itself.

**There is also a documented no-daemon-change resolution.** #4337 is close to a duplicate of this issue and was closed by its own reporter after they read the same history. Their actual problem was prompt asymmetry: ad-hoc delegated briefs did not carry the "open or update a pull request when ready" completion contract that issue-intake workers get, so no PR appeared and the existing PR-owning-worker auto-injection never engaged. Adding that footer closed their loop with no lifecycle change.

**Adjacent active work.** #4676 / #4574 add a cloud `worker:report` scope and deliver a worker report into the parent orchestrator's conversation, explicitly cloud-gated. That is agent-initiated rather than lifecycle-driven and does not cover local sessions, but it does occupy the `ao report` name and the worker → orchestrator delivery seam, as does #4411 / #4488. Whatever direction is chosen here should probably be consistent with those.

**Defect in my own PR, independent of direction:** #4968 adds migration `0127_orchestration_event_outbox.sql`, but `main` already has `0127_session_permissions.sql`. That is a duplicate goose version — the same failure as #3037, which was itself caused by the first version of this feature. I will renumber and rebase; I am not asking for review until that is fixed.

### The question

Before I put more work into #4968, which of these does the project actually support?

1. **No daemon-initiated orchestrator turns at all** — the #3038 / #3394 position stands, the answer is prompt-level completion contracts plus existing worker-targeted auto-injection (#4337's fix), and this issue should be closed as working-as-intended.
2. **Daemon-initiated turns are acceptable if the semantics are honest and opt-in** — i.e. emitting `worker_turn_settled` and never inferring task completion, deduplicating on transitions rather than re-firing, and gated per project or per session so it is off by default. If so, is opt-in gating sufficient, or is there a further bar the two reverted attempts did not clear?
3. **Neither — the orchestrator should pull, not be pushed** — a supported, documented subscription/callback contract so an external supervisor can react, with no daemon-authored writes into the orchestrator pane.

I am happy to implement whichever of these you want, or to close this and #4968 if the answer is (1). I would rather ask now than land a third version of a feature that has been removed twice.

## Reproduction: direct `ao send` is not a safe worker→orchestrator fallback for local Pi TUI

I reproduced a destructive shared-composer race in an isolated Scratch/Pi canary. No input was sent to the live human/orchestrator session.

### Environment

- Installed desktop reports `0.12.11`; `go version -m .../daemon/ao` identifies revision `7e8a662296d6d3015e89766007b4bb92937d6a23` (the v0.12.11 tag). The originally suspected v0.12.10 tag is `ed88a86d12027e0e37aa793d2f016165dde18e83`.
- Current `main` inspected at `9c271fc0a24c3c88ab89a3b8ec12eaacd19ed0c2`.
- Pi 0.85.0, macOS arm64, local TUI session using AO's `pty-host` runtime.

### Exact reproduction

1. Spawn an isolated Pi TUI canary and wait for `activity_state=idle`.
2. Through the canary's normal raw terminal-input protocol, enter `HUMAN-DRAFT::` **without Enter**, modeling a human's in-progress draft.
3. Run:

   ```sh
   ao send --session scratch-10 --message 'AGENT-REPORT::collision-canary'
   ```

4. Inspect the canary's persisted Pi JSONL.

Observed persisted user messages:

```text
Canary only. Reply READY, then remain idle. Do not modify files or contact other sessions.
HUMAN-DRAFT::[from dew-app-54] AGENT-REPORT::collision-canary
```

The human draft and automated report became one submitted user message. AO's `latest_user_prompt` recorded only the automated prefixed message, so that field does not expose the corruption.

### Transport trace

This is expected from the current implementation:

- local CLI `backend/internal/cli/send.go` prefixes `[from $AO_SESSION_ID]` and POSTs `/sessions/{id}/send`;
- `session_manager.Manager.send` routes **TUI** sessions through `sessionguard.DeliverWithPostWrite`;
- the runtime `SendMessage` writes literal terminal text, waits 300 ms, then writes Enter (`tmux` and `pty-host` do the same operation);
- current `InputLease` is a mutation fence/count, not an exclusive human-vs-automation lease. Human terminal input and automated `ao send` can both be admitted, and an already-present editor draft is not represented in durable activity state.

The same TUI transport exists in v0.12.10, v0.12.11, and current main. Current `sessionguard` protects permission/startup/switch states, but `idle` means only that the agent is not running; it does **not** mean Pi's composer is empty.

### Alternatives checked

- **Local `ao report`: unavailable.** Installed v0.12.11 says `unknown command "report"`; current main has no report command/API. PR #4488 is an open, currently conflicting foundation PR and explicitly excludes coordinator delivery/context injection.
- **Pi RPC / `pi.sendUserMessage`: capable but not wired for AO TUI.** Pi RPC supports accepted/queued `prompt`, `steer`, and `follow_up`; the extension API supports `pi.sendUserMessage(..., {deliverAs})`. AO's Pi TUI adapter launches interactive `pi`, not `--mode rpc`, and its managed `ao-activity.ts` extension exposes no authenticated IPC listener. Thus the daemon has no supported route to those APIs in a running Pi TUI.
- **AO Chat mode: collision-free.** Current `sendChat`/`RelayChatTurn` creates an automation-origin conversation turn and durably queues while busy; it never mutates a local composer draft. For Pi this requires separately installed pi-acp plus explicit bypass-permissions admission, and AO documents that Pi cannot currently hand off between TUI and Chat, so it is not a safe retrofit for existing orchestrators.
- **Cloud parent-message/report API: not a local solution and still draft-blind in PR #4676.** It is cloud-only and unmerged. Its active-parent path queues, but an idle parent takes the terminal fast path (`EncodeTerminalInput(text)`), where idle still does not prove an empty composer. It can reproduce the same logical concatenation.

### Required acceptance / suggested fix

Please treat collision freedom as a delivery invariant for this issue; replacing `ao send` with `ao report` is not sufficient if report flush later pastes into an idle TUI.

1. Add a per-session **human draft/input lease** recognized by every automated pane-writing path. From the first human edit until submit/clear, automation must queue or fail closed. The current `InputLease` only fences exclusive session mutations and allows concurrent admitted writers; merely serializing individual `Write` calls does not protect a draft already in the editor.
2. Prefer provider-native delivery where available. For Pi TUI, extend the managed Pi extension with authenticated session-scoped IPC that calls `pi.sendUserMessage`/queue APIs, rather than synthesizing keystrokes. Pi RPC is another option only if AO owns Pi through RPC instead of simultaneously treating stdin as a human TUI.
3. For durable `ao report`, piggyback pending reports into the same orchestrator turn when the human submits, and use provider-native/Chat queueing for independent wakes. Never flush by blind paste+Enter while a TUI draft may exist.
4. Add a regression test matching the canary: place an unsubmitted human draft, deliver an automated report, assert the draft remains unchanged and no combined user message is submitted; then prove deterministic queued delivery after submit/clear.

Related but distinct: #2342 fixed paste submission reliability. This defect is competing writers sharing one composer, even when paste+Enter works perfectly.

I verified this against the current PR head `5da61fab78fac396e3801585b203241b9b35b99a` using the exported `workspacewatch.Watch` API with real Git repositories and real filesystem notifications.

### Result matrix

| Scenario | Parent commit `86c023249` | PR head `5da61fab` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workspace nested beneath an unrelated Git repository | Times out waiting for a nested edit | Emits the change event |
| Genuine Git workspace opened through a symlink | Emits the change event | Times out waiting for the nested edit |

So the original bug is real and this PR fixes that scenario, but the symlink-root regression is also real and is introduced by this change.

Minimal symlink reproduction:

1. Create a Git repository containing an existing `src/main.go`.
2. Create a symlink whose final path component points to that repository.
3. Call `Watch(ctx, symlinkPath)`.
4. Edit `symlinkPath/src/main.go` and wait for the returned change event.

The base emits an event; the PR head times out consistently. Git canonicalizes `rev-parse --show-toplevel` to the real path, while `root` remains the symlink path. `sameWorkspaceDir` compares those path strings, returns false, and selects the `WalkDir` fallback. `filepath.WalkDir` does not descend through a symlink root, so nested directories remain unwatched.

Please compare the two existing directories by filesystem identity (for example, `os.Stat` plus `os.SameFile`, or carefully resolved paths) and add this symlink-root regression test.

Two smaller cleanup notes from the original review also remain:

- `sameWorkspaceDir` has one call site, while `AGENTS.md` says not to add one-off helper abstractions.
- The new nested-parent test configures `user.email` and `user.name` but never commits, so those calls are unnecessary.

## Confirmed live: parallel checkout races the agent, and the failure is swallowed (review findings #1 + #3 reproduced)

Reproduced end to end on a nodeops orchestrator session (this PR combined with the provider/orchestrator/terminal PRs, checkout ordering unchanged from this PR). Pulled the worker log directly from the sandbox:

```
"worker bootstrapped" harness=claude-code repository_url="https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git"
ERROR "background workspace startup failed"
      error="prepare repository checkout: existing workspace is not a Git repository"
```

### Mechanism
`startInteractiveAgent` and `prepareWorkspace` run concurrently in the same directory (`/workspace/repository`). The coding agent (claude) starts first and writes its project-local `.claude/settings.local.json` into that directory. `PrepareCheckout` then runs `git clone` into the now non-empty directory, which fails with "existing workspace is not a Git repository". This is the clone-races-the-agent-in-the-same-cwd case (review finding #3).

### Consequences (all observed)
1. The failure is swallowed: it is logged at ERROR but never surfaced, and `MarkWorkspaceReady` is never called, so `HoldAgentInputUntilWorkspaceReady` never releases and the user's keystrokes are held rather than delivered to the agent (review finding #1). In the UI this looks like typing that appears and then gets wiped.
2. The workspace stays empty (only `.claude` is present), so the orchestrator surveys `/workspace/repository`, finds no code, and reports the repository as empty even though it has content.
3. No error reaches the user; the session simply looks stuck or empty.

### Suggested fix
- Make the checkout tolerate a non-empty workspace: `git init` + `git remote add` + `git fetch` + `git checkout` into the existing directory, or clone into a fresh temp directory and move the contents in. That removes the ordering dependency entirely.
- Alternatively, prepare the workspace before launching the agent so the agent never writes into the directory ahead of the clone.
- Either way, surface the checkout failure to the session (and consider not gating agent input forever when the workspace never becomes ready) instead of swallowing it, so a real checkout error is visible rather than presenting as an empty repo plus dropped input.

## Bug (to fix on this branch): provider-availability check runs before the auto-link override

Found while testing the combined branch (#4624 + #4912 + #4676 + this + terminal fix) on a nodeops-only staging CP.

In `createSession` (`cloud/internal/httpapi/resource_handlers.go`), the provider-availability check from #4912 runs early:

```
if request.Provider != "" && !slices.Contains(s.availableSandboxProviders, request.Provider) {
    // 422 provider_unavailable
}
```

but this PR's auto-link override (which sets `request.Provider = orchestratorProvider` for a worker whose project has an active orchestrator) runs later. So the check validates the client-sent provider, not the value the worker will actually use after inheriting the orchestrator's provider.

### Repro
- CP offers only nodeops. Project has a nodeops orchestrator.
- The app's client-side sandbox-provider store still holds a stale `coder` selection (for example from earlier testing on a multi-provider CP; the store is initialized once at app start and does not re-read cleared localStorage).
- UI "Create a new task" sends `provider: coder`. Result: **422 provider_unavailable**, even though the worker would auto-link to the nodeops orchestrator and inherit nodeops.

Orchestrator-spawned workers are unaffected (they inherit the parent provider server-side), and the orchestrator spawn from the app reads localStorage fresh so it is also unaffected. Only the UI new-task path hits this.

### Fix
Move the provider-availability check to run **after** the auto-link override, so it validates the final resolved `request.Provider`. An auto-linked worker then passes because it inherits the orchestrator's (always-available) provider; standalone workers and orchestrators are still validated against the client-sent value.

## Caught in the wild, with the artifacts. This corrects two things I said earlier.

Reproduced on a maintainer's machine at **12:09 on 2026-09-06**, running `0.12.12-nightly.202609061620` — i.e. **a build that already contains #4849**. Same string as the original report:

```
Code signature at URL file:///Users/…/dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop.ShipIt/update.jfge6Sv/Agent%20Orchestrator.app/
did not pass validation: code object is not signed at all
```

I inspected the machine directly while the state was still live.

### 1. Correction: this failure never reaches ShipIt

`ShipIt_stderr.log` covers **2026-08-31 → 2026-09-06, 254 lines**, and contains **zero** occurrences of `did not pass validation`. Not truncated away — the log spans the failure and has no error of that class at all.

So the verification that fails is **`SQRLUpdater.verifyUpdate` running inside the app process**, on the freshly extracted bundle, *before* any ShipIt install request is created. ShipIt never sees it. My earlier framing of this as "ShipIt rejects the staged bundle" was wrong, and the note that Squirrel verifies in `SQRLUpdater.verifyUpdate` was right.

That matters: the corrupt window is between **the app's own unzip and the app's own verify**, in one process — much tighter than a cross-process ShipIt race.

### 2. The download was byte-perfect

The cached zip was still on disk:

```
size on disk:   176720977      feed: 176720977
sha512 on disk: eg2fkdgnU1WVSUIwfMp+NYp9oUikhczhgZP8C/jFLgldvsx4P8BmrbFRTERlx1tHh+x+eygZw71zE9HfiyJwjg==
sha512 in feed: eg2fkdgnU1WVSUIwfMp+NYp9oUikhczhgZP8C/jFLgldvsx4P8BmrbFRTERlx1tHh+x+eygZw71zE9HfiyJwjg==
```

Exact match on both. The bytes that failed to verify were correct bytes.

### 3. The same zip verified clean one minute later

`update.jfge6Sv` (the failing staging dir) was gone; `update.049tddx` had been created at 12:10 from the same cached zip. Running `SecStaticCodeCheckValidityWithErrors` against it with Electron's patched Squirrel flags (`kSecCSCheckNestedCode | kSecCSStrictValidate | kSecCSCheckAllArchitectures` = `0x19`) and the running app's designated requirement:

```
0x19 → PASS      (staged version 0.12.13-nightly.202609061848)
```

Complete bundle, executable present, 8 frameworks, 11 GB free disk. A ShipIt install request followed at 12:10:54.

**Same source bytes. One extraction fails, the next passes, ~60 seconds apart.** This is transient and self-healing, matching #4175 exactly.

### 4. #4849 worked, but did not fix this

ShipIt install requests per day from the same log, against actual installs:

| Day | Install requests | Installs |
|---|---|---|
| 08-31 | 25 | 0 |
| 09-01 | 49 | 1 |
| 09-02 | 5 | 1 |
| 09-03 | 2 | 0 |
| 09-04 | 23 | 2 |
| 09-05 | 17 | 1 |
| **09-06** (0.12.12, has #4849) | **3** | **1** |

The re-staging storm is gone — 17–49/day down to 3. But the signature failure still happened on that day, with only three requests. **So ShipIt request volume is not the trigger**, and my earlier "concurrent ShipIt instances" hypothesis does not survive this. Whatever races the extraction lives in the app process.

### Where that leaves the diagnosis

Established beyond reasonable doubt now:

- Not the published artifact (hash-verified against the feed, twice, on two machines).
- Not the download (byte-perfect on disk at failure time).
- Not disk space (11 GB free).
- Not ShipIt, and not a cross-process staging race.
- **A transient fault in the app-process extract→verify step, which a retry clears.**

Still unknown: what perturbs that first extraction. The remaining candidates are all inside the app process — overlapping stage operations sharing the cache directory, or an external agent touching `~/Library/Caches` between `ditto` finishing and `SecStaticCodeCheckValidityWithErrors` running.

### Fix implications

1. **The recovery path in #4981 is the right shape and now has direct evidence**: on this error class it discards the staged build and cached download so the next check re-downloads and re-verifies. The natural retry that succeeded here is exactly that behaviour, arrived at by luck.
2. **But it is more expensive than it needs to be.** The cached zip is provably intact — re-downloading 176 MB to fix a bad *extraction* is wasteful. A targeted improvement is to re-extract and re-verify from the existing verified zip before discarding it, and only re-download if that also fails. Worth its own issue; it needs an electron-updater path that does not exist today.
3. **Retry once before surfacing the error.** The user saw a red signature failure for a fault that cleared itself 60 seconds later. Even without (2), a single silent re-attempt would have turned this into a non-event.

## 1. "Telemetry cleanup failed. Reporting remains disabled while cleanup retries." — confirmed bug, High confidence

This shows for **every Windows user** in Settings → General. It is not caused by anything the reporter did.

What happens:

- The General tab's telemetry row renders this message when the telemetry policy state is `cleanup_failed` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/GeneralSettingsSection.tsx` in 0.12.12, key `settings.telemetryEvents.failed`).
- On Windows the policy file store hard-codes itself as unsupported: `this.durabilitySupported = (options.platform ?? process.platform) !== "win32"` (`frontend/src/main/telemetry-policy-file.ts:67` in 0.12.12, still present on `main`).
- Because of that, every policy load on Windows comes back unacknowledged. `DesktopTelemetryController.initialize()` maps "acknowledged but not applied / not durable" to `cleanup_failed`, and the row shows the failure message.
- Nothing actually failed. Telemetry-off is the intended state on Windows. The UI just has no honest "not available on this platform" state, so it shows a permanent error instead.
- Side effect: a 1-second interval retries cleanup whenever the state is not `applied` (`desktop-telemetry-controller.ts` in 0.12.12 wires `setInterval(... retryPendingCleanup, 1_000)` in `main.ts`). On Windows that retries a guaranteed-to-fail path every second, forever.

Fix direction: render a neutral "telemetry preferences aren't supported on Windows" state when `durabilitySupported` is false, and skip the retry loop for that case instead of looping on it.

Thanks @rafeautie — that's a very useful data point, and it reframes the diagnosis. If killing the orphaned `ao.exe` and deleting the `.db` files cleared **all three** original symptoms (controller stopped, telemetry cleanup failed, reopening window), then the likely story is:

- An `ao.exe` from an earlier install survived an uninstall and kept running (this issue)
- The old daemon kept serving stale state from its old `.db` while the new app talked to it — producing the controller/telemetry weirdness
- Removing the process and its DB gave the new install a clean slate, and everything works

So the primary bug is this one: **uninstall leaves the daemon running and the data behind.** [#5018](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5018) (visible console window killing chat sessions) may still be real, but it's no longer confirmed as what hit this machine.

Two things worth noting from the code for whoever picks this up:

- The NSIS config (`frontend/makers/maker-nsis.ts`) has no `deleteAppDataOnUninstall` setting either way, and AO deliberately keeps all state in `%USERPROFILE%\.ao` (daemon DB, worktrees, running.json). Uninstall doesn't touch it, and a running `ao.exe` isn't killed by the uninstaller — it's a detached process not parented to the app.
- The app does have an orphan-kill fallback on quit (`process.on("exit")` in `main.ts`), but that only covers app-owned daemons — a keep-alive daemon (`AO_KEEP_DAEMON=1`) is deliberately left running across quits, and a daemon orphaned from a previous install has no supervisor to kill it.

Fix direction for #5033: NSIS uninstaller should (1) attempt a graceful `POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/shutdown` / taskkill on `ao.exe` before removing files, and (2) either delete `%USERPROFILE%\.ao` or offer a checkbox for it. Keeping the data by default is defensible (it holds session worktrees), but silently leaving a running daemon is not.

Marking the original issue's diagnosis accordingly — the reporter (same person) confirmed symptoms cleared after cleanup, so #5030 is effectively resolved for them pending the #5033 fix.

Normal behavior confirmed: closing the app **should** kill `ao.exe` (the app owns the daemon via a supervisor link and has an orphan-kill fallback on quit). So the state you hit was the abnormal one. Most likely sequence, based on the code:

- A previous app instance quit abnormally at some point (crash, forced kill, update mid-run) in a way that skipped both the graceful shutdown and the orphan-kill fallback — leaving `ao.exe` running with no supervisor.
- Or the daemon was running in keep-alive mode (deliberately survives app quit) and was never stopped before uninstall.
- Then the uninstaller removed the app files but knew nothing about the detached `ao.exe` or `%USERPROFILE%\.ao` — so the old daemon kept serving stale DB state to your fresh install. That matches all three symptoms, and why deleting the `.db` files + killing the process cleared everything.

1. **A relative `AO_DATA_DIR` makes the shim point to the wrong place.** With `AO_DATA_DIR=data` and a shared install directory, the new code puts `data/runtime/ao-path/...` on PATH. When the agent starts in its worktree, that relative path is resolved from the worktree instead of the daemon's data directory. Additional datapoint: the reject-vs-sanitize divergence described here also bites a **tmux path on macOS** — the reviewer pane — not only conpty on Windows.

`reviewerHandleID()` (backend/internal/review/launcher.go:237-239) builds the reviewer runtime handle as a raw concatenation `"review-" + workerID` and passes it to `runtime.Destroy`/`Create`. Unlike the worker-pane path, it never goes through `SessionName()`'s sanitization; it lands in the `handleID()` validator (tmux.go:1164-1171, pattern `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` at tmux.go:48), which **rejects** dotted ids instead of sanitizing them.

Live failure on a dev build (project id `axisrow.github.io`, so session id `axisrow.github.io-38`):

```
launch reviewer: reviewer replace stale pane:
tmux runtime: invalid handle id "review-axisrow.github.io-38"
```

Result: `ao review trigger` → 500 `REVIEW_OPERATION_FAILED`, review run row goes straight to `status=failed` — for every session of any project whose id contains a dot, on macOS/tmux. Worker sessions of the same project spawn fine because their panes go through `SessionName()`.

So the inconsistency is not just tmux-vs-conpty across platforms: within tmux itself, one path sanitizes (`SessionName`) and another rejects (`handleID` fed by `reviewerHandleID`). Sanitizing in a shared layer as proposed here would fix both; the reviewer handle specifically needs `reviewerHandleID()` to stop bypassing it. Full repro and stack details are in the fork issue: axisrow/agent-orchestrator (reviewer pane handle / dotted project ids).

## Independent reproduction and root cause (Windows)

I hit this on a different machine and build, and traced it to a specific pre-launch
admission check. Summarising here because the root cause looks orthogonal to #5017.

**Environment:** AO `0.12.12` (stable) · Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200 (x64) ·
Codex CLI `0.151.0` (standalone) · `claude-code` `2.1.150`. Same symptom set as the
report: instant `CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE`, survives a full daemon
restart with a fresh pid, `ao agent ls` shows `codex installed authorized`
throughout, and `--agent claude-code` spawns fine in the same project.

The daemon's own API surfaces the underlying reason:

```json
POST /api/v1/agents/codex/accounts/ensure → 503
{"error":"unavailable","code":"CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE",
 "message":"Codex account setup did not complete",
 "details":{"reasonCode":"account_storage_unsafe","retryable":false}}
```

### Call chain

```
bootstrapInner()                        codex_account_reconcile.go
 → cleanupPendingCredentialHomes()      codex_account_catalog.go
 → ensurePrivateDirectory(pendingRoot)  codex_account_catalog.go
 → validateCodexDirectoryAncestors()    codex_secure_fs_windows.go  ← first statement
 → ancestor walk reaches the volume root C:\
 → codexWindowsPathMetadataIsSafe() == false
 → errors.New("codex directory ancestor ACL is unsafe")   // plain error
 → bootstrapStorageFailure() → bootstrapFailure("account_storage_unsafe", false)
```

`ensurePrivateDirectory` calls `validateCodexDirectoryAncestors` as its **first**
statement, before `os.MkdirAll`. `bootstrapInner` runs both
`cleanupPendingCredentialHomes` calls before `reconcileGlobal`, so this fails before
`reconcileGlobalInner` reaches `AccountFactory.Open`. **Neither Codex nor the
account-scoped app-server is ever started** — no process is spawned, consistent with
the error returning instantly.

### ACL evidence

The walk validates through the volume root. On my machine every AO-owned level
passes and `C:\` is the first failing ancestor. Evaluating `C:\` the way
`codexWindowsHandleSecurity` does:

| ACE / property | Value | AO's evaluation |
|---|---|---|
| Owner | `NT SERVICE\TrustedInstaller` | **`ownerTrusted = false`** |
| `Authenticated Users` | `0x00000004` (`FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY`), not inherit-only | **counted, intersects `codexWindowsMutationMask`** |
| `Authenticated Users` | `0xE0010000`, `INHERIT_ONLY` | correctly **skipped** — not a factor |
| `BUILTIN\Users` | `0x001200A9` (read/execute) | passes, correctly not a factor |
| `SYSTEM`, `BUILTIN\Administrators` | `0x001F01FF` | trusted, pass |

Two things worth being precise about: the inherit-only `0xE0010000` ACE is already
ignored by the `INHERIT_ONLY_ACE` filter and should not be cited as a cause, and the
ordinary read/execute `BUILTIN\Users` ACE is correctly accepted. `ownerTrusted =
false` alone short-circuits `codexWindowsAncestorACLIsSafe`, so the owner check fails
independently of any ACE.

I can only speak to my own machine here — I haven't inspected the original
reporter's filesystem permissions, so I'm not asserting this is the same failure they
hit, only that the symptoms match and this path fails first when it applies.

### Current `main`

I diffed `v0.12.12` against `main`; these are byte-identical, so the behaviour is
unchanged on `main`:

- `codex_secure_fs_windows.go` (`validateCodexDirectoryAncestors`, `codexWindowsHandleSecurity`)
- `codex_windows_security.go` (`codexWindowsAncestorACLIsSafe`, mutation mask, trust predicates)
- `codex_account_catalog.go` (`ensurePrivateDirectory`, `cleanupPendingCredentialHomes`)
- `codex_account_reconcile.go` (`bootstrapInner`, `bootstrapStorageFailure`)

### Why the obvious workarounds are wrong

**Changing ownership or ACLs on `C:\` is not an acceptable workaround.** It is a
machine-wide OS security change to satisfy one application, and a
TrustedInstaller-owned volume root with a default `Authenticated Users`
`FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY` ACE is a normal Windows configuration. I deliberately left
the machine unmodified.

**Adding `TrustedInstaller` to the trusted-owner set is not sufficient on its own.**
It would clear `ownerTrusted`, but the non-inherit-only `0x4` ACE still intersects
`codexWindowsMutationMask` and would fail `codexWindowsAncestorACLIsSafe`.

### The invariant worth preserving

After validation, no untrusted principal should be able to directly mutate the
private vault, replace an already-existing component used to reach it, or redirect
resolution through a reparse point.

Mapping that onto Windows directory rights, substitution of an existing component
`C` under parent `A` needs two distinct rights:

- **gating:** `DELETE` on `C`, or `FILE_DELETE_CHILD` on `A`. Rename is the sharp
  edge here — unlike `RemoveDirectory` it does not require the directory to be
  empty, so a principal with either right can relocate an existing component
  wholesale and interpose a replacement at the same path.
- **completing:** `FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY` on `A`, which alone can only create a
  *previously unused* name (`CreateDirectory` on an existing name returns
  `ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS`).

`WRITE_DAC` / `WRITE_OWNER` matter because they let a principal grant themselves the
gating rights; note the owner implicitly holds `WRITE_DAC`, which is why ancestor
ownership is worth checking at all.

By that analysis the current ancestor policy rejects several rights that do not
confer substitution over an existing component: `FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY` (`0x4`) and
`FILE_ADD_FILE`/`FILE_WRITE_DATA` (`0x2`) only add new names, and — worth checking
against the generic mapping rather than assuming — `FILE_GENERIC_WRITE` maps to
`READ_CONTROL | FILE_WRITE_DATA | FILE_APPEND_DATA | FILE_WRITE_EA |
FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES | SYNCHRONIZE`, containing no `DELETE`, `FILE_DELETE_CHILD`,
`WRITE_DAC` or `WRITE_OWNER`. `GENERIC_ALL` maps to `FILE_ALL_ACCESS` and does
include them.

### Fix design space

I'm deliberately not proposing a patch — I haven't built or tested one, and this is
security-policy code where a plausible-looking design can be wrong. Offering the
constraints instead:

- the private **vault** policy should stay strict and unchanged;
- ancestor policy is a genuinely different problem from vault policy and probably
  warrants its own predicate and its own rights mask, focused on
  replacement/substitution rights rather than reusing the vault mutation mask;
- structural validation (is a directory, `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT` clear) needs
  to be retained on every component — that is what defends against redirection;
- whether a system-servicing owner such as `TrustedInstaller` should be trusted *for
  ancestors only* is a policy call for maintainers, but the volume root cannot
  satisfy vault-grade ownership on stock Windows.

One caution from my own analysis, in case it saves someone the detour: I first
considered stopping the strict walk at a trust anchor (e.g. the AO data root) and
applying only structural checks above it. **That is unsound.** If an untrusted
principal holds `FILE_DELETE_CHILD` on the anchor's parent, they can rename the
entire anchor aside — contents intact, its own ACL irrelevant — and create a
replacement at the same path. There is a real instance of this shape on stock
Windows: the inherit-only `0xE0010000` ACE on `C:\` maps to
`GENERIC_READ|GENERIC_WRITE|GENERIC_EXECUTE|DELETE` and propagates to child objects,
so a directory created directly under `C:\` inherits an ACE granting
`Authenticated Users` `DELETE` on it. Any relaxation should keep a per-component
rights check rather than trusting a boundary.

I haven't tested any variant against the suite, so I can't speak to what it does to
existing behaviour beyond the paths I traced.

### Test coverage

There is no `codex_secure_fs_windows_test.go`, and the ancestor walk and its
termination appear to have no direct coverage. The Windows tests in
`codex_windows_security_test.go` are pure-predicate unit tests over synthetic inputs
— `TestWindowsAncestorACLPolicyAllowsReadButRejectsMutation` passes
`ownerTrusted: true` and a single synthetic ACE, so it cannot observe a
TrustedInstaller-owned root or a real `0x4` ACE.

A test that would have caught this has to exercise the **real** ancestor chain up to
the volume root rather than a synthesized ACL: create a vault under a normal temp
directory, apply `protectCodexPrivateDirectory`, and assert
`validateCodexDirectoryAncestors` returns nil on a stock unprivileged Windows
runner. Worth pairing with a junction-substitution case (junctions need no admin) so
the reparse defense stays honest if the ancestor policy is relaxed.

### Diagnosability

`bootstrapStorageFailure` classifies anything that is not an `*os.PathError` /
`*os.LinkError` as `account_storage_unsafe`. The ancestor rejection is a plain
`errors.New`, so it lands in that bucket and the real cause — which ancestor failed,
and which predicate — never reaches the surface. That matches the request in the
issue body for the underlying bootstrap failure to be named; propagating the failing
path and predicate would turn this into a short diagnosis rather than a source trace.

account-scoped app-server launches without the resolved Codex directory on `PATH`,
it can fail during initialization while the daemon still resolves Codex fine. Worth
having on its own merits.

That said, I reproduced #4989's symptoms independently on Windows (AO `0.12.12`,

Evidence for two of the bullets here, since this issue is the existing tracker for the exact symptom.

**"Mergable should not show a loader" / "Review pending should show loader"** — reproduced, root-caused, and fixed in #5082 (bug write-up with screenshots in #5081).

**Symptom:** an idle session card in the **Ready** lane renders a green `Mergeable` label with an animated loader ring spinning beside it, continuously, for as long as the card is mounted.

![board card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-board-mergeable-spinner/.issue-assets/board-mergeable-spinner/card-2026-09-08.png)

**Root cause** — `packages/product-ui/src/SessionsBoardView.tsx:245-251` (against `ddf1e54f`):

```ts
const showStatusLoader =
    !needsAttention &&
    session.displayStatus !== "Needs human review" &&
    (session.status === "working" ||
        session.status === "review_pending" ||   // <-- the label never sees this
        ...);
```

The label reads `displayStatus`; the loader reads `status`. The daemon derives those from opposite ends of a session's PR set — `displayStatus` from the **best** PR (`contract/kanban.go`, `kanbanPriority`, `ready` first), `status` from the **worst** open PR (`contract/status.go`, `aggregatePRStatus` + severity table). A session with one mergeable PR and one still awaiting review therefore shows the best PR as text and the worst PR as an icon. The predicate has no `session.activity` term, so an idle agent cannot switch it off, and `animate-spin` is `spin 1s linear infinite` with no terminating state.

**Deterministic repro** (fails on `ddf1e54f`, passes on #5082):

```
status: "review_pending", displayStatus: "Mergeable", kanbanColumn: "ready",
activity: { state: "idle" }
=> AssertionError: expected SVGSVGElement{…} to be null
   received <svg class="lucide lucide-loader-circle mr-1 size-icon-2xs animate-spin">
```

**Fix in #5082** keys the loader off the label the card actually renders, honouring the intent stated here rather than removing loaders wholesale:

- `Review pending` **keeps** its loader (as this issue asks).
- `Mergeable` / `Approved` / `Merged` lose it.
- A genuinely working agent (`status === "working"`) still spins, even on a `Mergeable` card.
- `status` remains the fallback only when the daemon sent no `displayStatus`.

Presentation only — the daemon's multi-PR aggregation is deliberate and unchanged.

The remaining bullets here — sidebar status dots, "closed with merge" in red, and the wider "go over where we show loader" sweep — are **not** covered by that PR and keep this issue open.

## Reproduced again: Codex login-shell browser command selects June 27 CLI

**Source:** user report in AO session `agent-orchestrator-322`, 2026-09-07 America/Los_Angeles (2026-09-08 UTC). Reporter supplied a screenshot of the inspector remaining on Summary with the Browser activity badge. No public chat URL supplied.
**Analyzed against:** `ddf1e54f18f9e27dacbfa0d1d90ce37a1c37228e`, also current origin/main at investigation time.
**Confidence:** High. **Priority:** existing P1 retained.

### Reproduction and evidence

Inside the same macOS/zsh Codex worker, execute `which -a ao` and `ao version` with login-shell execution enabled versus disabled:

- Login shell: `~/.local/bin/ao` wins; symlink target `~/.cache/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/bin/ao`; version `dev-local commit 5fa53ad9 built 2026-06-27T13:57:21Z`.
- Non-login shell: `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao` wins; version `dev`.
- Both status probes reach the actual Go daemon, ready on port 3001. Checking the port alone is therefore insufficient to detect stale CLI selection.
- Login-shell `ao browser open https://aoagents.dev/` fails with `unknown command "browser" for "ao"` before any browser request.
- The absolute bundled executable with the same arguments succeeds for this session, returning the correct page URL/title; a subsequent browser snapshot succeeds too. No missing browser capability in this reproduction.

The original tool invocation separated the browser command and source reads with semicolons, so successful trailing reads obscured its failure at the overall shell exit-status level. The worker consequently misreported browser inspection as unavailable.

### Mechanism and fix direction

`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:4252` supplies the launch PATH pin via `HookPATH`; `backend/internal/agentlaunch/env.go:20` prepends the canonical directory. The pin works in the inherited non-login environment, but does not survive the nested login-shell environment. This confirms the already documented launcher/login-shell boundary rather than a browser-controller regression.

Retain the existing fix scope: a canonical executable reference usable by agent tool shells and managed guides, safe handling/diagnostics of stale AO-owned launchers, and a regression covering a nested login shell that prepends an incompatible ao. Do not overwrite arbitrary user executables or disable shell initialization globally as an unverified workaround. For this worker, using the absolute bundled executable restores browser access immediately.

### Separate sidebar behavior: intentional, not the failed command

Even a successful open does not automatically select Browser. `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx:1332` badges unseen activity and keeps the selected inspector tab. This was deliberately introduced by [PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146), commit `30a7c20f6`. The supplied screenshot is consistent with that behavior; it alone does not establish whether a page loaded. Restoring automatic reveal would be a separate UX decision, not a fix to CLI resolution.

No speculative code change in this triage. The workaround was verified against the running desktop; existing landing-page changes in the worker are unrelated and remain local.

### Architecture

All eight ACP bindings now inherit persistent ownership from the shared ACP driver. There is no provider allowlist or fallback to daemon-owned session processes. Provider-specific protocol, version, permission, and launch behavior stays in each binding; short-lived catalog discovery is explicitly separate.

The review also fixed host-replacement event-ID collisions, acknowledgement past failed SQLite projections, queued dispatch before completion acknowledgement, and explicit teardown after a controller has detached/disappeared. Failed fresh setup/branch publication releases its host; failed live adoption preserves the existing owner. The updater uses actual daemon-reported ownership.

Reviewed at 92f54e8e2cfc87f5477750a94d1b126e4c934fb3. The reported stale-filter issue is real, and deriving the effective filter centrally fixes the normal case. I found two edge cases worth addressing before merging:

1. **P2 — A failed project-list poll can reactivate a previously rejected filter.**

   In `lib/projectFilter.ts:19–27`, an empty list returns the saved ID. Since `getSessions()` converts `/projects` failures to `[]`, the fallback can undo itself after a successful recovery. I reproduced this with the actual helper and a saved ID of `removed`, one listed project `remaining`, and one worker belonging to `remaining`:

   | Poll | Applied filter | Visible workers |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Successful `/projects` | `all` | 1 |
   | Failed `/projects` → `[]` | `removed` | 0 |
   | Successful `/projects` again | `all` | 1 |

   The new filtered empty state provides an escape, so this is an incomplete recovery rather than a claim that the original implementation handled it better. Still, a transient project-list failure should not restore a filter already known to be invalid. Could we retain the last successful project list, scoped to the paired machine, and distinguish loading/failure from a successful empty response? A success → failure → recovery test would cover this gap.

2. **P2 — Automatic spawn reseeding bypasses the existing project-change resets.**

   In `app/spawn.tsx:89–101`, invalidating and reseeding `projectId` leaves `model`, `modelTouched`, and `agentTouched` intact. Consider opening the sheet on project A, explicitly choosing a model, then removing A while the sheet remains open with B as the only remaining project. The effect switches the sheet to B, but the old explicit model still wins in `displayedModel` and can be passed to `spawn()`; a touched agent also prevents B's agent defaults from being selected.

   Manual project selection already handles this through `resetModelSource()` and `setAgentTouched(false)` in `selectProject()` at lines 175–181. Could automatic invalidation/reseeding apply the same resets? A component/state-transition test should verify that removing the selected project and reseeding another does not carry the previous project's explicit model or agent-selection state. This finding is based on tracing the component's state and submit paths, not a device reproduction.

| Session deleted (404) mid-transition | stopped after 15.4s | stops after 0.34s |
| Stranded transition, then an app switch | budget silently refilled, 6 calls to 10 | no refill |
| Rotated password (401), two app switches | — | 4 requests total, one per foreground |
| #4122 session, healthy link | 11 calls, stops | unchanged |

Moving the count into `failureRef` does more than close the refill: the tap recheck and the poll loop now share one count, so a tap during an outage no longer resets the backoff the loop is sitting on. The `setPollable(true)` on foreground behaves as its comment claims — one request per app switch under a 401, which is well clear of the five-failure lockout.

I also checked the two things most likely to break quietly: `InlineBanner` already takes `secondary`/`onSecondary` (the pending-send banner uses both), so the new chat banner is not a typecheck risk, and the dropped `interfaceTransitionFailureAttempts` export has no consumers left.

### The readiness bound does not hold on a failing link

`nativeSessionReadinessAttempts = 10` is documented as the terminating condition for a wait that is not guaranteed to clear. It is not one when requests fail.

`readinessRef.current.attempts` is incremented only on the `result?.ok` branch, which is deliberate and right — a run of timeouts teaches you nothing about whether the native session became ready, so it should not spend the window. But now that failures no longer terminate either, a readiness wait against an unreachable daemon has nothing left to stop it. Simulating an hour on `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED` with every request timing out: 183 requests, `attempts` still 0, still scheduled. It runs for as long as the screen is open.

At roughly 3 requests a minute and gated on `appActive` this is a long way from the 60/minute the PR started at. The problem is the invariant rather than the rate: the comment above the constant says "poll until it resolves" has no terminating condition, and on a bad link that is still the behaviour.

The two waits are not the same shape and I do not think they should share a retry policy:

- A live transition is a real in-flight operation with a user watching a banner. Retrying it until the link returns is correct, and is exactly what the last commit fixed.
- A readiness wait is speculative. #4122 says it may never clear even when everything is healthy, which is why it was given a budget in the first place.

Letting failures consume the readiness budget, or putting a wall-clock bound on that specific wait, closes this without touching the transition path.

Same root cause, worth deciding on deliberately: a persistent 5xx also polls forever at the 8s ceiling (79 requests over 10 minutes in the harness). "A 5xx is a fact about the link, not the session" holds for a proxy or a restarting daemon, but a daemon panicking in this one handler is a fact about the session too.

### Smaller things

- The new `if (mobileInterfaceTransitionIsActive(status.transition)) return;` is a silent no-op after the user has watched a spinner. The transition card appearing covers it, so this is about how the tap reads rather than what it does.
- `onSecondary={recheckingTransition ? undefined : ...}` still fires `haptics.tap()` on a press of the disabled "Retrying…" label. The existing Cancel does the same, so this may be worth fixing in both or neither.
- `fetchFailed` is in the poll effect's dep array but is no longer read in the body. It is load-bearing — it is what re-runs the effect after a mount fetch that never landed — but a future dependency cleanup would drop it as unused and silently break cold-start recovery. A line in the dep array or in the `fetchFailed` comment naming that would keep it.

1. **Unknown vs observed zero, end to end.** `UnresolvedThreadCount` is now a pointer through the contract, DTO, and CLI DTO. An observed zero serializes explicitly (`*int` + `omitempty` only drops nil), and the CLI keeps the summary field as a pointer so a pre-change daemon's successful-but-fieldless response stays unknown: the table renders `-` and JSON stays `null`, never a known-looking `0`. Update: we later pinned a concrete mechanism behind this exact `Error: Session ID ... is already in use.` loop, in a related restore path.

**Root cause found (workspace-name encoding mismatch in the transcript probe):**
- Claude Code encodes every non-alphanumeric character in the `projects/<dir>` transcript directory name — underscores included — while our transcript probe only mirrored `/` and `.`.
- For any workspace path containing an underscore, the probe derived a different directory name than claude itself uses, so it misdiagnosed an existing conversation as missing.
- `GetRestoreCommand` then returned `ok=false`, and the restore path fell through to the fresh-launch fallback, which pins the same deterministic `--session-id` over a live transcript.
- `--session-id` is create-only (continuation requires `--resume`), so claude exited with "Session ID ... is already in use." — and every retry repeated the same fallthrough, matching the kill+restore loop described here.

**Fix:** locate the `--resume` transcript by scanning the projects directory instead of encoding the path (no longer mirroring claude's encoding rules), so restore correctly returns `--resume` for an existing conversation and never falls through to the occupied `--session-id`. Both affected sessions recovered with plain `ao session restore` afterwards; a daemon restart is not required for the recovery itself, only to pick up the fix.

This may not be the only path to this error (the original report followed an OOM crash, ours followed a termination sweep + restore), but the "same UUID retried forever with no CLI-side lock visible" shape matches exactly.

Related data point for the restore path here: we hit `Error: Session ID ... is already in use.` on restore in a way that looked like a stale CLI-side claim but turned out to be a transcript-probe encoding bug — the probe mirrored only `/` and `.` when deriving the `projects/<dir>` name, while Claude Code encodes every non-alphanumeric character, so underscore-containing workspaces made the probe misdiagnose an existing conversation as missing and fall through to the fresh-launch fallback that pins the (create-only, already occupied) `--session-id`. Details in https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4280#issuecomment-5595677924 — the fix was to locate the `--resume` transcript by scan instead of path encoding. Worth keeping in mind alongside the `sessionIDPattern` fix in #3876: both are "session-id derivation disagrees with what claude accepts/knows" classes.
