Technical notes, for anyone reading the diff.

Conversation updates still use the `session_updated` event. The payload adds `itemSequence`, `itemRevision`, and `headSequence`. No chat text goes in the change log. The client treats a sequence as the live page only when it is the current head or the next row, and that row is inside the newest loaded page. A gap, an older page, or a missing sequence invalidates every loaded page. Updates coalesce for 150 ms, and one full refresh in that window wins over a head refresh.

Streamed prose deltas for the same kind, item, turn, and conversation sit in memory until 32 events, 8 KB, or 40 ms. `ProjectCoalescedProviderEvents` archives them and appends the joined text in one transaction. Provider events stay unacknowledged until that commit. A replay that finds the archive rows already present does not append again. A store that does not implement the batch interface still writes one event at a time.

`ao.lastSession` in renderer localStorage holds the session id, project id, title, and incarnation. The incarnation is `session.createdAt`, which is what the draft scope already uses. `StartupSessionDraft` writes the composer draft and submits nothing. After the daemon is ready, a successful workspace list navigates to that session once. A missing session is forgotten. A resolved non-session route, after restore is done, forgets the record so quitting from the board does not force the old session. A failed workspace query does neither.

`resolveDefaultBranchTargets` still runs before the worktree is created, from the local ref. `applySymlinks` still runs before the agent starts, and a link failure still aborts spawn. `FetchDefaultBranch` runs in `scheduleDeferredSpawnWork` after the runtime exists. The fetch uses the existing 5 second budget.

`releaseColdSessionCopies` removes React Query keys for sessions other than the open one and the one just left. The prefixes are conversation, models, config, skills, editor handoff, reviews, and the source and workspace file queries. It does not touch the workspace list, dispatch tracking, or local echos. Terminal buffers live outside React Query.

Playback is `useSmoothStreamingText`. The chunk pattern is `/\S+\s+/`, then a 10 ms delay, matching Vercel `smoothStream` word mode. Text already present on first paint stays put. Later growth releases one finished word at a time. `streaming: false` or reduced motion flushes the buffer. Reasoning text uses the same hook. The copy button reads `message.text`, not the partially shown string.

generation stores an opaque int64 ordering token for each model-catalog refresh attempt.

  - Seeded from UTC UnixNano().
  - Shared by writes from the same refresh.
  - Newer generations may overwrite older ones; stale generations are rejected by SQLite.
  - Retry callbacks verify the generation still matches before running.

  It prevents a slow, older discovery from overwriting newer cached models. It is not a model version or count—treat it only as a monotonic freshness fence.

### Could we reuse the existing handoff state machine?

Could you investigate whether the local and Cloud implementations can share one interface-handoff core instead of maintaining two separate state machines?

The existing local implementation already defines the durable phases and terminal-state rules:

- [Local transition model](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0be2146992ea63ff02861f74cc234f23645ce43e/backend/internal/domain/session_interface_transition.go#L41-L84)
- [Local transition runner](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0be2146992ea63ff02861f74cc234f23645ce43e/backend/internal/session_manager/interface_transition.go#L362-L470)

This PR introduces substantially the same vocabulary and progression again:

- [Cloud transition model](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/8ed46637354e74c5fbf8ee2411ba014814ca73f1/cloud/internal/domain/session_interface.go#L56-L88)
- [Cloud transition coordinator](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/8ed46637354e74c5fbf8ee2411ba014814ca73f1/cloud/internal/interfacereconcile/coordinator.go#L208-L286)

Both implement approximately:

```text
requested
→ preflighting
→ draining
→ source_stopping
→ source_stopped
→ target_starting
→ activating
→ completed / failed / recovery_required
```

The storage and execution mechanisms genuinely need to differ:

```text
Local:
  SQLite + direct process/PTY control

Cloud:
  PostgreSQL + leases + remote worker commands
```

However, the phases, validation, allowed transitions, terminal-state decisions, and failure/recovery rules appear to be domain logic rather than storage or transport logic.

Cloud already depends on the backend module ([`cloud/go.mod`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/8ed46637354e74c5fbf8ee2411ba014814ca73f1/cloud/go.mod#L5-L7)) and already reuses public backend packages such as [`pkg/agentruntime`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/8ed46637354e74c5fbf8ee2411ba014814ca73f1/cloud/internal/workerexec/command.go#L14), so sharing a public handoff package appears mechanically possible.

Could you investigate whether we can extract something like this?

```text
shared handoff core:
  phases, policies, validation
  next transition/action
  failure and recovery decisions

local adapters:
  SQLite store
  direct process driver

cloud adapters:
  PostgreSQL store
  leased scheduler
  worker-transport driver
```

I am not suggesting that Cloud call the current internal `runInterfaceTransition` method verbatim; it contains local process-specific behavior. The question is whether its environment-independent decisions can be extracted and used by both implementations.

If a shared coordinator is not feasible because Cloud requires leases and restart-safe distributed scheduling, could we at least share a pure transition reducer/state table and run the same conformance tests against both adapters? If even that is not possible, please document the concrete local-versus-Cloud invariant that requires two independent implementations.

Technical notes from the run.

Archive goes through the same kill path as the archive button. When git status is dirty, StashUncommitted writes refs/ao/preserved/<session id> through a temporary index. git add -A does not pass -f, so gitignored files are skipped. The log on all 20 sessions was skipped_count=1.

The session_worktrees row is written with that ref and state active before the folder is removed. A removed row is what shutdown uses to put edits back on the next boot. An archive snapshot uses active so reopen does not apply it.

Restore checks out the existing local branch. It does not apply the snapshot. A missing local branch returns SESSION_BRANCH_MISSING and does not build a branch from the snapshot. The ref stays.

"Put saved edits back" runs git cherry-pick --no-commit of that snapshot. A clean apply deletes the ref. A conflict leaves markers and keeps the ref. No commit is created.

If the worktree has unstaged edits on the same lines, cherry-pick exits before it writes anything. The old code treated that as a conflict and left only the newer text. The fix captures those edits with git stash create --include-untracked, which writes a commit object and does not update refs/stash. It then runs git merge-tree --write-tree and git read-tree --reset -u. Overlapping lines get conflict markers. Ignored files stay out.

The 4.69 GiB numbers above are from a local run of 20 sessions, 240 MiB ignored each. That run is not in CI.

CI runs TestArchiveDropsIgnoredCheckout. It uses one worktree and a 1 MiB ignored file. Archive must delete the checkout, git must not grow by that file, restore must come back clean on the same commit, and an unstaged edit on the same lines must leave both versions with conflict markers and no new commit.
